I will do it much like last year, with a few small adjustments. I have 10.1 mu and the land all runs in wheat-maize rotation, so the same 10.1 mu goes to wheat first and then maize after wheat harvest. I have done this many years, and around here if fertilizer is too short, the ears are small and the grain is light, so I do not like to cut it too hard. But money is tight too, so I will not throw fertilizer blindly. For wheat, I will use improved seed, the kind people around here have been planting these years, because it stands better and yields steadier than old seed. Wheat needs a stronger base fertilizer, especially phosphorus, and I will still topdress nitrogen at jointing. Since I have well water, I will give wheat about 3 irrigations if the year is normal: one over winter or at turning green depending on moisture, one at jointing, one at filling if the land is dry. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because neighbors planting hybrid get fuller cobs and more grain. Maize eats nitrogen hard, so I will keep nitrogen a bit higher than wheat, with part under the seed and part chased later. Potash I will not leave out, because if maize falls over or the stalk is weak, it hurts harvest. Pesticide I will do only as needed but I usually end up spraying wheat more times than maize. On 10.1 mu, I will keep rotary tillage because it is quicker and cheaper for my size, and it fits the wheat-maize turnover time. If the season is normal and water is there, I will aim for roughly 950 jin wheat and 1200 jin maize per mu, maybe a little more in a good year.
